g181: An _ separates the prefix and index; an existing trailing underscore is not duplicated. No files are made for unselected targets. Once an index is reserved, partial failure does not reuse it automatically; renaming and deletion do not roll it back.
g182: Do not change targets or storage rules during recording. Stop in {{APP_NAME}} ends only this logging block’s segment and keeps CANoe measurement running. A shared start button does not guarantee identical start times or synchronization across devices.
g183: Keep CANoe’s lightning (measurement) on and repeat Start recording → Stop and save → Start next recording in {{APP_NAME}}. Each start automatically checks measurement, so no connection recheck is needed after turning on the lightning. Recheck after changing the cfg, logging block or structure.
g184: CAN and Diag stop the selected block, complete the current BLF’s final buffer and header, then check and archive it. If CANoe completes the file only at the next trigger, the app briefly switches to a separate internal file and stops it to complete the current BLF. Measurement and other blocks continue. Internal switching files are not user logs and consume no extra index. After Archived, use the same button for the next recording. A file can be archived while a handle remains open if a complete stable copy can be made. Large files can take longer to check and copy.
g185: .vil_work is an internal work folder separating active or finalizing files from completed files. Finished BLF and PCAP files are archived under their final names in your output folder. The app does not delete the work folder or merely patch a header to label an unfinished BLF as valid.
g186: Stop / archive needs confirmation does not mean the file is absent. Generated files are preserved when stopping, completeness or archiving cannot be confirmed. Changing or truncated files are not marked complete. Inspect the actual files and failure in recovery; send a bug report if it keeps failing.
g187: Initial filenames come from the cfg and are not fixed. CANoe trigger numbering can produce suffixes such as _T002 or _T002_T001 after restoration. Restoration handles trigger suffixes in the same original folder and name; arbitrary other field-code substitutions are not guaranteed. Do not change filenames or options during capture.
g188: If CANoe keeps the last internal switching file open, .vil_work may remain briefly. Archived files are kept; internal files are cleaned up when handles are released. Temporary files from segments interrupted by X or an unexpected exit are deleted; locked-file cleanup is retried. Interrupted history does not block the next recording.
g189: If CANoe rejects the original cfg output name, the app may report Output restoration deferred · You can continue recording. Once it verifies the stopped block belongs to {{APP_NAME}}, the next recording is allowed; final BLF checking and archiving still apply. The original cfg is not saved automatically. Do not save a deferred temporary output path into the CANoe configuration. This exception does not apply after external block, filename or option changes, or manual recording.
g191: Log folder beside the main capture-target heading opens your configured capture output folder. Previous capture files, Operation history and Delete previous share one row, with Operation history immediately left of Delete previous.
g192: Press Enter in the previous filename field or click Rename to use the entered name without adding an index. Extensions remain and Diag adds _Diag. Example: Drive log.blf and Drive log_Diag.blf. Renaming is unavailable during recording or file processing.
g193: Check paths in Delete previous before deleting. Confirmed permanent deletion bypasses the Recycle Bin. Operation history is read-only and shows rename/deletion results with original and changed paths. Use Log folder above to open the configured save location.
g194: .vil_work is temporary storage for recording and validation. Segments interrupted by X or an unexpected exit are cleaned up automatically; completed final files are kept. Do not delete it yourself during recording or file processing.
g195: Processing may be deferred for files still in use, externally changed or not confirmed closed. Check Operation history and the actual paths. Settings, index and history are stored per PC and Windows user. On first launch after fully closing AutoLog, its old profile is copied to the new {{APP_NAME}} profile. Custom paths, prefixes, indices and rules remain; only the old default prefix changes to One_Click_Log. The original database and capture files are not moved or deleted.
g197: Recent activity shows about 4–5 lines and retains the latest 500 entries. Scroll inside the list for earlier entries. Filter by all, warnings/errors or errors; hover over an entry for its timestamp, original message and details. The copy button and entry count were removed.
g198: Main-screen communication monitoring, recording quality and packet viewer controls, and the environment-check control in settings, were removed. Open saved captures in Wireshark for packet analysis. Use the gear to configure connections.
g199: Settings → Zipy validation includes a default rule checking the 2-second average reception of packets whose Source MAC starts with 02:00:00. Other sources and protocols are also saved: this is not a capture filter. Defaults are 2-second startup grace, 2-second no-data timeout and minimum 100pps. After startup grace, reception below the minimum for 2 seconds also stops capture. Adjust to the equipment’s normal traffic; 0pps disables only the rate floor. Deleting a rule disables its reception monitoring. Actual CAN / Diag reception monitoring is currently unsupported.
g200: On the first launch after updating to 0.9.17 or later, a missing default rule is restored once. Old default times of 5s / 3s become 2s / 2s; the identified manual replacement named “zipy activation check” is removed. Other custom rules and edited timeout values remain. Later intentional deletion is respected. Use Restore default to reset its conditions, timing and popup text while retaining other rules. If all 16 slots are used, delete one rule first. After saving, the default rule is selected; changes apply from the next recording.
g201: A confirmed selected-network disconnection, rule violation or recorder error stops all selected targets together; properly closed files are checked and archived. An observed violation remains a stop reason even if traffic recovers before the next UI update. Unavailable monitoring interpretation or response for 5 seconds also stops capture. Recent activity and bug reports retain the cause; the session is not marked fully successful. Check cables, hardware and settings, then use the green Start new recording button. An upstream cable break that leaves the adapter link up is detected through required-source reception monitoring. Internet connectivity is not a criterion. Use 한 | EN | 中 at the top to switch the app language.
g202: The default rule is named “Zipy activation failed”. A confirmed violation displays a popup independently of file finalization. Its default message says: “Zipy data activation failed. Enter the following command in the Render terminal: |6 → e1”. Edit per-rule messages and line breaks or add guidance for new rules in Popup message. A blank message uses general guidance. Saved rule names and messages are displayed exactly as stored, regardless of the app language; editing is locked during recording. The same failure in one segment does not repeatedly open popups. Open popups do not block file processing or main-window X exit.
g203: For CAN / Diag, stopped CANoe measurement, a stopped selected block or unavailable CANoe response / recording status triggers a “Recording interrupted” popup and stops all selected recording targets. It identifies affected targets and detected causes, combining simultaneous failures into one alert. The app attempts to archive properly closed files and records results in Recent activity. Waiting for acknowledgement does not delay file processing or X exit.
g204: This detects stopped CANoe measurement or recording, for example after removing CAN hardware USB or power; it does not directly inspect physical wiring. If only the vehicle-side CAN wire is disconnected while CANoe keeps measuring and recording, automatic detection is currently unavailable. Actual CAN / Diag reception monitoring is unsupported. Absence of a popup does not prove reception: check CANoe Trace. After an alert, check USB, power, cables, CANoe licenses and compilation errors; restore F9 measurement and Trace reception before starting a new recording.
g209: Follow section 2 to allow CAPLcompExec and CANoe, then restart CANoe and recompile. Ask your PC administrator if company policy blocks this.

g217: Check that the entire ZIP was extracted, tools/Wireshark exists and Npcap was installed separately. If using another installation, check its selected path and companion tools. Restart after driver installation, and check the cable and adapter selection.
g219: Check actual frames in Trace and assign the correct DBC to that message’s CAN channel. A DBC on a different channel will not decode the expected signals. Check the DBC version and signal definitions against ECU software. With measurement kept running between segments, the first frame may be later than time zero; select the time range containing actual frames.

g231: Closes {{APP_NAME}} and its dedicated CANoe windows from this run, without switching to tray or background operation. Unfinished segments are discarded and completed files retained. If cleanup stalls, force-exit follows after about 1 second; another X forces immediate exit.
g233: When a problem occurs, click Bug report at the top.
g235: Email the file to Taegon.Kim with the time, selected targets, button sequence and, if relevant, CANoe Write errors. The app does not send email automatically.
g236: Developer logs are always rotated in developer_logs beside the EXE. The default rotation threshold is 5 MiB per file, with the current file and up to four backups retaining about 25 MiB. Retention depends on size, so no duration is guaranteed. Relaunching from the same folder appends to the existing logs; the oldest records are replaced as the limit is reached.
g237: If the UI is unresponsive for over 5 seconds, execution locations and thread stacks are written once to the same rotating log. Packet contents and variable values are not recorded. Sending a bug report after responsiveness returns helps locate the stall.
g239: Supplied logs reviewed on 2026-10-23: Two Diag BLFs captured with 0.9.16 contained Extend/L9 diagnostic requests and positive responses through their ends. In one, 155 frames across about 39ms present in the simultaneous CAN file were absent from Diag; the cause is unresolved. The other had no omissions within the compared range. Normal exit, valid file structure and successful diagnostic actions do not guarantee lossless CAN capture.
g240: Main-window X closes {{APP_NAME}} and all dedicated CANoe windows opened in this run. It does not hide to tray or keep running in the background. If cleanup stalls, force-exit follows after about 1 second; another X forces immediate exit. Closing settings or Operation history closes only that window.
g241: To keep a recording, finish stopping and archiving on the main screen first. X discards unfinished segments and cleans temporary files. Completed final files, settings and the next index are retained. Owned files that cannot be deleted immediately, for example because they are locked, are retried on the next launch without blocking new recordings. No manual recovery of the previous unfinished segment is required after relaunch.
g242: Dedicated CANoe processes are identified by handles created in this run. X immediately sends termination signals without waiting for their windows to close. The original cfg is not saved automatically. Independently launched CANoe and Wireshark windows are not closed. Save needed channel mapping and project changes yourself before recording.
g243: Before updating, finish stopping and archiving any recording you want to keep, close the old {{APP_NAME}}, and use the entire new release folder. Since 0.9.11, old unfinished history is cleaned up automatically. After relaunch, connect the cfg and check F9 and Trace before a new recording. Previously completed captures are retained.
g244: Per-PC settings, indices and history are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\{{APP_NAME}}. On a new PC, verify old paths and NIC selections. Validate the PC’s disk, tools and vehicle setup with short recordings before longer tests.
g245: Validation scope for this release{{APP_VERSION}} includes regression checks for setup discovery, signatures/hashes, cancellation/failures, ZIP content equality, existing-file protection, raw preservation on failure and saved settings. Qt screenshots and the offline guide are updated in three languages. Actual administrator installation, COM changes, new-PC connections, vehicle acquisition, high load and long-duration trials remain separate. The known Diag gap still needs investigation; file validity does not establish lossless acquisition.

The app does not automatically delete exported ZIPs or limit their count or age, so retain and organize them separately. Compression normally makes the ZIP size differ from the source logs.
g269: Save a ZIP immediately after an issue and provide the TC ID, trial, occurrence time and timezone, selected targets, recording index, action sequence, expected result and actual result. Include CANoe Write errors and screenshots when relevant. Actual BLF, PCAP and PCAPNG files, the full cfg, settings/history database and screenshots are not attached automatically. Receive loss or diagnostic exchanges require the relevant original captures and a comparison reference.
g270: Orderly shutdown drains pending diagnostics to disk. The X deadline, an abnormal exit or PC power loss can omit the last records. When possible, save a ZIP before closing and another immediately after restarting. If the app cannot respond, preserve a copy of developer_logs from that execution folder. Moving to a new release folder does not automatically merge the previous folder logs into a new ZIP.
g271: Diagnostics record operational state and errors and redact designated packet-content fields. File paths and general error strings are not fully anonymized. Storage, permission or diagnostic-queue errors can lose records, so a ZIP alone cannot prove every action or lossless acquisition.
g272: For long tests, retain ZIP snapshots and original captures at segment boundaries. Extrapolating diagnostic growth during short real-use samples from 0.9.12 and 0.9.16, about 25 MiB corresponds to roughly 10 to 20 minutes of continuous recording. This is not a long-duration measurement or guarantee for current 0.9.21; repeated actions, selected targets and errors may shorten retention.
g273: The Initial_Setup.bat beside the EXE combines CANoe 19 registration and Npcap setup. Save and close the app and all CANoe windows, then double-click it. Existing Npcap files skip installation; otherwise the internal installer is checked by hash and signature before elevation. Review the official license and options.
